gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured latency figure for a wireless 75% magnetic board under $100: HLPlanet's OSLTT readings are 0.60 ms wired / 0.75 ms on 2.4 GHz for the Gamakay TK75 TMR and 0.65 ms wired / 1.01 ms on 2.4 GHz for the Yunzii RT75 Pro, and KitGuru's 240 fps test found the Epomaker HE75 V2 no faster at 8,000 Hz (15.96 ms) than at 1,000 Hz (14.46 ms).
standout_why: Compared against Notebookcheck's HE75 Mag review (cited), keebspicks (cited), HLPlanet's Hall-effect guide, HLPlanet's HE75 Mag review and setupinsider's under-$100 page. Notebookcheck gives no latency in ms, only '1,000 Hz max tested via wireless' for the older HE75 Mag. keebspicks says it does not test and prints brand figures. HLPlanet's guide gives OSLTT figures mostly for boards over $100 and, among the candidates, only 'under 1ms' for the wired-only MCHOSE Jet 75; it has no figure for the Yunzii RT75 Pro, Gamakay NS75, Gamakay TK75HE V2 or Epomaker HE80. HLPlanet's HE75 Mag review and setupinsider derive latency from polling rate. The RT75 Pro and TK75 TMR figures sit on separate HLPlanet review pages and the HE75 V2 figures on KitGuru, none of which were in ChatGPT's results. The cited Tom's Guide and PC Gamer pages and the RTINGS 75% list came back truncated, so they were not compared. ChatGPT's own answers say the polling rates are 'not independently measured latency'.
decides: It confirms rather than overturns. On the one named bench that measured both (HLPlanet, OSLTT), the Gamakay TK75 TMR (ours, under $100 through our link today) has the lower 2.4 GHz figure, 0.75 ms against 1.01 ms for the Yunzii RT75 Pro, and a near-equal wired figure, 0.60 against 0.65 ms. That gives the TK75 TMR an honest 'lowest measured wireless latency among the under-$100 boards with a named measurement' segment; it is a TMR-sensor magnetic board, which the page should say. ChatGPT's 'best overall' Epomaker HE75 V2 has no bench latency, only KitGuru's end-to-end camera test, where 8,000 Hz gave no gain and KitGuru's spec list says '1,000Hz recommended'. All gaps are under 1 ms, so the measurements support the pick but should not be sold as decisive. No named measurement was found for the Gamakay NS75, Gamakay TK75HE V2, AULA Hero 75 HE, AULA F75 HE or Epomaker HE80.

findings.label: Single-key latency, HLPlanet (Marcus Richardson), OSLTT
findings.note: Review dated 2026-05-18. OSLTT (Open Source Latency Testing Tool) times keycap contact to signal receipt by the computer. Number of runs is not stated. No Bluetooth figure. The review lists 8,000 Hz wired and 2.4 GHz, 1,000 Hz Bluetooth, and a price of $119.99 at the time. The page's own path is /gamakay-tk75-tmr-review/.

findings.label: Single-key latency, HLPlanet (Marcus Richardson), OSLTT
findings.note: Review dated 2026-01-02. Each figure is an average of 10 tests. No Bluetooth figure. The review states 8,000 Hz polling and a 128K scan rate without describing how they were checked. Yunzii's store page claims 0.1 ms wired / 1 ms wireless, so the wired measurement is 0.55 ms above the claim and the 2.4 GHz one matches it. The page's own path is /yunzii-rt75-pro-review/.

findings.label: TK75 TMR against RT75 Pro on the same reviewer's bench
findings.value: TK75 TMR is 0.05 ms lower wired and 0.26 ms lower on 2.4 GHz
findings.note: Arithmetic: 0.65 - 0.60 = 0.05 ms wired; 1.01 - 0.75 = 0.26 ms on 2.4 GHz. Both HLPlanet OSLTT; the RT75 Pro figures come from https://www.hlplanet.com/?p=6800. The reviews are four months apart, and the run count is given only for the RT75 Pro.

findings.label: End-to-end click latency, KitGuru (Carlos Ribeiro), 240 fps camera test
findings.value: 14.46 ms wired and 16.54 ms wireless at 1,000 Hz; 15.96 ms at 8,000 Hz
findings.note: Review dated 2026-09-09. End-to-end figures include the PC and display, so they cannot be compared with OSLTT single-key figures. 8,000 Hz was 1.50 ms slower than 1,000 Hz wired (15.96 - 14.46). The review does not say whether the 8,000 Hz run was wired or wireless. Its spec list reads 'Up to 8,000Hz (1,000Hz recommended)' and gives connectivity as 2.4 GHz, Bluetooth and USB-C.
